added.text: The mod loader keeps a log in NeetLoader/logs/latest.log, and the previous session's log as previous.log.
Install a mod by dropping its folder into the game's Mods folder.
Mods that need other mods load after them, and are skipped with a clear message if something they need is missing.
A mod that crashes is logged and doesn't stop the other mods from running.
Mods can be switched off without deleting them.
Mods can be loaded, unloaded and reloaded while the game is running.
Mods that support it update by themselves when their files change, no restart needed.
The mod loader starts with the game by itself. No launcher, proxy DLL or Proton launch options needed.
One command installs the mod loader into the game, and one removes it again and restores the original files.
Check the install, the installed mods and whether the game is running with a single status command.
Send commands to the running game from a terminal or a script.
Start the game in a window and close it again from the command line.
Read the mod loader log and the game's own log from the command line, even while the game runs.
Editors and other tools that support MCP can launch, inspect and control the game for testing.
God mode: no dying and needs stay where they are.
Dev bridge mod: lets local tools read and change the running game for testing.
Mods can be reloaded, loaded and unloaded through the dev bridge, so a rebuilt mod can be tested without restarting.
Mod menu (F1) with a list of installed mods, their status and any errors.
Load, unload, reload and switch mods on or off from the mod menu.
Mod settings can be changed in the mod menu instead of editing files.
What's New screen in the mod menu that lists every change by version.
Dev Tools tab: god mode, refill needs, teleport, money, spawn any item, fire and power switches.
The mod menu opens What's New by itself the first time the game starts after an update.
The Mods page shows each mod's recent log lines, so problems are easy to spot without opening log files.
The framework and mods that other mods rely on can be reloaded too; a rebuild updates everything in place without restarting the game.
Mods can add new items that spawn, sell in the online stores and save like the game's own.
Mods can add new cards to the computer's anime card game.
Mods keep their in-game data when they are reloaded.
Twelve new Halloween cards in the anime card game, with spooky recoloured art.
Summon button on the card site: spend crystals for a random payout or a shiny card with free levels.
Auto-clicker you can buy with crystals that clicks every unlocked card for you.
Card Expansion settings in the mod menu: summon cost, shiny chance, auto-clicker price and speed, and the crystal exchange rate.
The pause menu has a MODS section with buttons for the mod menu and What's New, in the game's own style.
Saves are written in a compressed, open format (.nsav) that's about 16 times smaller; older saves still load.
Old save files are cleaned up automatically, keeping the newest 25 (adjustable).
Option to keep writing plain JSON saves like the original game.
Command-line tools to list saves and convert them between the compressed format and readable JSON.
Mods can build menus that use the game's own fonts, buttons and controls.
Mods can be split into features that switch on and off individually while the game runs.
The Mods page lists each mod's features with on/off switches.
Every website on the in-game computer can be given a different address.
Mods can add their own apps and games to the in-game computer, with start menu entries.
PC Apps page in the mod menu to see and change every computer app's address.
Pumpkin Smash: a whack-a-pumpkin game on the in-game computer that pays a little cash.
Cheat Menu mod: press Insert for god mode, needs, speed, teleport, money, crystals, spawning, fire, power, doors and game speed.
Open House mod: walk into the pantry and through the black basement door and dad's yard door, with optional switches for the attic, the roof and the demo's store limits.
Mods can add their own lines, choices and conversations to the game's dialogue.
Phone Expansion mod: new numbers to call and new calls that ring in, with choices that can deliver food, cut the lights, open doors and more.
Caller ID on the house phones shows who's calling while the phone rings.
Phone tab in the mod menu to see every new call and ring any of them.
New calls can be added with simple text files, no programming needed, and update as soon as the file is saved.
New numbers to call: Pumpkin Pizza (555-7492) delivers food, and the Scream Line (555-3666) has spooky facts and candy.
Spookbusters (555-2368) and Satan (666-6666) pick up properly when you call them a second time, and they have offers.
New calls ring in: a caller you shouldn't answer, mom when you're starving, and package tracking after store orders.
Dial 555-0100 for a test line that shows what new calls can do.
Unofficial NEET Patches mod: fixes for bugs in the game itself, each one switchable.

changed.text: Converting 10K crystals pays $5 instead of $3, and the amount can be changed in the settings.
Compressed saves, save cleanup, the feedback block and the pause menu MODS section are now separate features that can be switched off.
The mod menu now uses the game's own menu style.
Card Expansion's parts (spooky cards, summons, auto-clicker, exchange rate, promotion fix) can be switched on and off one by one.
Compressed saves and save cleanup are now the Open Saves mod, so they can be installed or removed on their own.
Blocking feedback reports is now the No Feedback mod.
Cheats moved out of the mod menu into the Cheat Menu mod, opened with Insert.
The framework and No Feedback are always on and can no longer be switched off or unloaded.
The fix for promoted cards losing their stats moved from Card Expansion to Unofficial NEET Patches.

fixed.text: The mod log no longer fills up with hundreds of copies of the same game warning.
MCP tools that talk to the game no longer fail with an internal error.
Removing a mod that added items or creatures no longer breaks loading the save.
A save with more anime cards than the game has loads instead of throwing an error.
Promoted anime cards keep their doubled earnings after loading a save.
Modded anime cards keep their level and unlock state after loading a save.
Saving works again with a dead house spider around, and dying no longer gets stuck because of it.
Story events like the thief's arrival no longer break after Grandpa dies, and no longer repeat every frame after an error.

removed.text: Sending feedback reports from the pause menu, since they would describe the modded game rather than the original.
